mushisamagic.caption:
The Jessica Lunsford case remains one of the most heartbreaking true crime cases in America. In February 2005, 9 year old Jessica disappeared from her bedroom in Homosassa, Florida. Weeks later, investigators found her buried in a shallow grave behind a mobile home where John Evander Couey had been staying. She was found clutching the purple stuffed dolphin she had taken from her bedroom that night. 

 
​What makes this case even more disturbing is what Couey later told investigators. In a recorded confession, he said Jessica was still alive when he buried her and that he let her keep her stuffed dolphin because she wanted to take it with her. Her cause of death was determined to be asphyxiation. The confession itself was later ruled inadmissible at trial because of a violation of his right to counsel, but other evidence was allowed to be presented. 

​John Evander Couey was ultimately convicted in 2007 of first degree murder, kidnapping, sexual battery on a child, and burglary. The Jessica Lunsford murder case shocked the country and helped push for stronger laws aimed at protecting children and monitoring convicted sex offenders. It is a case that still gets discussed today because behind all the courtroom footage and headlines was a 9 year old girl whose life was taken far too soon.

​What looks like remarkable coordination is also a reminder of how much patience daily commuting can demand.
